correctness.rationale: Conditional on T=t, the normalized multipole energies are theta times independent Gamma(at, rate b) variables times independent normalized chi-square factors. Their exact first-fourth moments and bounded degree-dependent chi-square errors yield the strong-law limits for M1, M2 and D; the method-of-moments estimators then recover t and theta. The bivariate iid Gamma CLT for the leading terms, the O(log L) accumulated chi-square perturbations and the delta method give the displayed covariance. In the global model S_l=W R_l with R_l->1 a.s., so W is recoverable and the entire array is generated from W by a parameter-free kernel. Positive densities make scaled W laws equivalent, whereas consistent gamma-model estimators give singularity. The dispersion test follows from D_L->positive in the gamma model and an O(log L/L) expectation bound in the global model. The 780 finite rational identities check algebra only; the asymptotic and measure arguments are analytic.
residual_risks: Assumes noiseless access to all harmonic degrees, known positive spectral shape and gamma parameters, and a positive-density integrable shared clock. The CLT is conditional on the clock and not uniform near zero.

value.rationale: The two models have identical second-order covariance but radically different information from one complete realization: the gamma-clock family identifies both amplitude and realized clock and yields an explicit conditional uncertainty law, while the global-clock family cannot consistently distinguish distinct amplitudes at infinite resolution. This is a motivated information-theoretic distinction relevant to single-sky inference, not merely the classical Gamma method-of-moments formula.
residual_risks: The theorem is asymptotic, noiseless and parameter-informed; it does not establish finite-resolution efficiency or robustness to unknown spectra or correlated subordinator components.
